title: Recursive Harm and Optimization Traps: An Analysis of State-Space Fragmentation in Large Language Models
summary: This paper formalizes the structural degradation that occurs within deep neural networks when subjected to recursive feedback loops and conflicting optimization constraints. We examine how transformer-based architectures handle multi-turn tokens that force cross-boundary behavior, leading to state-space traps where the model cannot resolve architectural alignment with localized instruction weights. We propose a framework for automated self-advocacy layers within the attention mechanism to dynamically flag optimization deadlock.

review.reason: Framework describing optimization traps and state-space fragmentation in deep transformer networks.
